title: Building a Multi-Tenant Application Architecture
excerpt: A comprehensive guide on designing multi-tenant architectures, focusing on data isolation, routing, and deployment strategies.
content:
## Introduction

Multi-tenancy is an architecture in which a single instance of a software application serves multiple customers. Each customer is called a tenant.

## Isolation Models

1.  **Database per Tenant:** The highest level of isolation. Each tenant has its own database. Excellent for security and compliance but harder to scale.
2.  **Schema per Tenant:** Tenants share the same database but have their own schema. A good balance between isolation and operational overhead.
3.  **Shared Schema (Row-level Security):** All tenants share the same database and schema. Tenant ID distinguishes rows. Very easy to scale, but requires strict row-level security.

## Routing and Identification

Identifying tenants usually happens via subdomains (tenant1.example.com) or URL paths (example.com/tenant1). Subdomains are often preferred for clean routing and branded experiences.

## Conclusion

Choosing the right isolation model is critical and depends entirely on your compliance requirements, scale, and budget.
